title: Why Do Le Mans Cars Have a Fin on Their Back?
description:
On the back of almost every Le Mans prototype from the last fifteen years, there is a tall, thin fin, like the fin of a shark. It does not make the car faster. It was added because racing cars were flying, literally, lifting off the ground at over three hundred kilometres per hour and somersaulting through the air. Today, ten parts of the cars that race for twenty-four hours at Le Mans, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

1:17 1. The shark fin
2:46 2. The holes above the wheels
4:01 3. The long tail
5:27 4. The chicanes on the straight

7:57 6. The glowing panels
9:15 7. The driver change
10:30 8. The hybrid front axle
11:45 9. The hidden ballast
13:02 10. The old Le Mans start
14:17 The verdict
